guidance_diff.why: The last two 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press releases for this name have not been pulled from EDGAR, so there is no mechanical guidance diff. This is the free substitute for a transcript: it carries the guidance figures and none of the questions.
guidance_diff.caveat: Mechanical. Two press releases, sentences with a forward-looking word and a figure, matched on metric and period. It does not read tone, it cannot see a guide given without a number, and a filer that changes how it names a period between releases shows one lapsed and one introduced where a reader would see one reiterated. The verbatim sentence sits under every row so the machine's reading can be checked.

tone.assessment: Not directly determinable. The note contains no management quotes, no call or transcript material, and no Q&A — searches for CEO, CFO, said, call, and transcript return nothing in the file. The only tone-adjacent signals are actions rather than language: management raised the 2026 WFE outlook, and the September guide of $8.1 billion sits about 20% above the $6.72 billion just reported. Read together those actions are forward-leaning, but that is an inference from figures, not an observation of how management spoke.
tone.evidence: Management raised the 2026 wafer fab equipment outlook to the low $150 billion range.
tone.confidence: low. It is not higher because the file records zero words attributable to management. Tone here is being reverse-engineered from a raised market outlook and an above-current-quarter guide, and the same numbers would be consistent with cautious delivery. The note also carries one countervailing forward statement it does not attribute to anyone — a December gross margin dip to 48.5% — which cuts against reading the quarter as uniformly confident.

new_risks.risk: Gross margin is guided down for the December quarter on mix and tariffs. At 48.5% this is 1.5 points above the note's own under-47% thesis killer, so the guided direction moves toward a stated exit condition without reaching it. Tariffs appear in the file only here, as a named margin driver.
new_risks.quote: The December quarter is expected to see gross margin dip to 48.5% on mix and tariffs.

new_risks.risk: Export controls carry an approximately $600 million revenue headwind for calendar 2026. This is not named in the bear case or among the thesis killers, and the note gives no duration, mitigation, or calendar 2027 exposure.
new_risks.quote: Export controls are about a $600 million revenue headwind for calendar 2026.

new_risks.risk: The September guide itself instantiates the bear case's own peak signal: $6.72 billion to $8.1 billion is roughly a 20% sequential jump, which the note's bear case describes as what peaks look like. The guidance is therefore simultaneously the quarter's strongest datapoint and a trigger the note pre-committed to reading as a warning.
new_risks.quote: A 20% sequential revenue jump is what peaks look like.

The note is a compressed summary rather than a transcript, so this may reflect what the note omitted rather than what management withheld.

dodged.reasoning: The file quantifies the headwind for calendar 2026 in a single sentence and never returns to it. There is no mitigation plan, no statement of whether it recurs or lapses, and no calendar 2027 figure, even though the note treats calendar 2027 as its key thesis-killer year.

read.market_reaction: The note records one price move around the report: "Stock rose 8% after hours after falling 7% during the day." It gives no closing price for that day, no follow-through beyond the after-hours session, and no volume or analyst-reaction detail. Separately, the screen line dated 2026-09-04 — roughly six weeks after the late-July report — puts the stock at $292.66, "-34% from 52 week high, -33% from all time high," with short interest 2.5% of float, forward P/E 25.3 against a 30.1 four-year median, and EV/EBITDA 42.2. The note does not connect that drawdown to the earnings report or date the high, so the path between the 8% after-hours move and the 2026-09-04 price cannot be reconstructed from the file. On positioning, the note places LRCX in the compounder bucket ("Bucket: compounder.") and treats cyclical as only "a near miss for the cyclical bucket at 33% off its high" — it does not classify this as a cyclical turn. The file contains no price target, no estimate-revision breakdown beyond the single line "Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved +20.1% in 90 days.", and no dated journal entry; its only forward price figures are the valuation scenarios "bear (2028 downturn) 16x on $6 is about $96; base 22x on $10 is $220; bull 26x on $12 is $312." The stated action is "Buy on pullback, November tranche, small. Buy zone $250 to $290. Conviction 3 of 5." with "Price trigger: $215." given as a bare number, not as a closing-price condition.

multiples.label: Forward P/E
multiples.basis_note: The two sides are not the same multiple. The left is a forward P/E, the Street's estimate of next year's earnings. The median on the right is trailing: the price at each fiscal year end divided by that year's reported diluted EPS. Where earnings are expected to grow, forward is mechanically lower than trailing, so this column reads cheap by construction.

multiples.label: EV/EBITDA
multiples.basis_note: Both sides are trailing, so this comparison is like for like.

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at 4 fiscal year ends, so it is a 4-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.
own_history.basis_warning: Read the P/E row with care. Across the 136 names that carry both comparisons, 85% print a negative 'vs median' on forward P/E with a median of -29%, against 50% and 0.0% on EV/EBITDA where both sides are trailing. That gap is the basis mismatch, not 136 companies being cheap. It is also correlated with growth: faster-growing names look cheaper here (rank correlation -0.28 against revenue CAGR, versus -0.15 for EV/EBITDA), because their forward earnings are further above their trailing ones. The score weights the like-for-like EV/EBITDA comparison more heavily for exactly this reason.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.
